Glossary of bird terms.question: corpuscles of _____-endings similar to the Pacinian corpuscle, found in the mucous membrane of the tongue, in pits on the beak and in other parts of the bodies of birds
Glossary of bird terms.fact: corpuscles of Herbst Nerve-endings similar to the Pacinian corpuscle, found in the mucous membrane of the tongue, in pits on the beak and in other parts of the bodies of birds.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: About one half of bird species with fovea have a single one, but uniquely in birds, some, such as terns, kingfishers and _____, have a second fovea, called the temporal fovea, that assists in judging speed and distance and increases visual acuity
Glossary of bird terms.fact: About one half of bird species with fovea have a single one, but uniquely in birds, some, such as terns, kingfishers and hummingbirds, have a second fovea, called the temporal fovea, that assists in judging speed and distance and increases visual acuity.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: A hard or fleshy plate extending from the base of the upper mandible over the forehead of several bird species including some water birds in the rail family, especially the gallinules and moorhens, swamphens and _____, as well as in jacana
Glossary of bird terms.fact: A hard or fleshy plate extending from the base of the upper mandible over the forehead of several bird species including some water birds in the rail family, especially the gallinules and moorhens, swamphens and coots, as well as in jacana.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: pileum As defined in the treatise Manual of Ornithology: Avian Structure and Function, the "entire top of the head, including the forehead, crown and _____." pin feather Also, blood feather
Glossary of bird terms.fact: pileum As defined in the treatise Manual of Ornithology: Avian Structure and Function, the "entire top of the head, including the forehead, crown and occipital regions." pin feather Also, blood feather.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery

Glossary of bird terms.fact: crest feather Collectively, the/a crest.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: Other birds having distinctive crissum colouration include _____'s thrashers and grey catbirds
Glossary of bird terms.fact: Other birds having distinctive crissum colouration include Le Conte's thrashers and grey catbirds.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: dietary classification terms (-vores) _____ may be classified by terms related to the types of foods they forage for and eat
Glossary of bird terms.fact: diastataxis The state of lacking a fifth secondary feather on each wing, which occurs in birds in more than 40 non-passerine families. In these birds, the fifth set of secondary covert feathers does not cover any remex.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: The -vore suffix is derived from the _____ vorare, meaning 'to devour'
Glossary of bird terms.fact: The -vore suffix is derived from the Latin vorare, meaning 'to devour'.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: The albumen protects the yolk and provides additional nutrition for the embryo's growth, though it is made up of approximately _____ water in most birds
Glossary of bird terms.fact: The albumen protects the yolk and provides additional nutrition for the embryo's growth, though it is made up of approximately 90% water in most birds.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: It is especially common among Psittaciformes, with an estimated _____ of captive parrots exhibiting the disorder

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: flight feather Also, _____ volatus
Glossary of bird terms.fact: flight feather Also, Pennae volatus.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: fovea _____: foveas or foveae
Glossary of bird terms.fact: fovea Plural: foveas or foveae.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: From the _____ for "little fork", the furcula is a forked bone, also found in some dinosaurs, located below the neck and formed by the fusion of the two clavicles
Glossary of bird terms.fact: From the Latin for "little fork", the furcula is a forked bone, also found in some dinosaurs, located below the neck and formed by the fusion of the two clavicles.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: As the thorax is compressed by the flight muscles during a downstroke, the upper ends of the furcula spread apart, expanding by as much as _____ of its resting width, and then contract
Glossary of bird terms.fact: As the thorax is compressed by the flight muscles during a downstroke, the upper ends of the furcula spread apart, expanding by as much as 50% of its resting width, and then contract.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: gleaning _____ cases: foliage gleaning; hover-gleaning; crevice-gleaning
Glossary of bird terms.fact: A specialized stomach organ found in the digestive tract of some birds constructed of thick muscular walls that is used for grinding up food, often aided by particles of stone or grit. gleaning Specialized cases: foliage gleaning; hover-gleaning; crevice-gleaning.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: Some birds, such as the common chiffchaff of _____ and the Wilson's warbler of North America, feed actively and appear energetic
Glossary of bird terms.fact: Some birds, such as the common chiffchaff of Eurasia and the Wilson's warbler of North America, feed actively and appear energetic.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: It is a feature found on many male hummingbirds, particularly those found in _____, whose gorgets are typically iridescent

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: Examples of _____–Parkes terminology versus traditional terminology may be seen in the entries for prealternate moult and prebasic moult

Parkes to make the terminology for describing bird plumages more uniform. Examples of Humphrey–Parkes terminology versus traditional terminology may be seen in the entries for prealternate moult and prebasic moult.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: The most common pattern involves flying north in the northern spring to breed in the temperate or _____ summer, and returning in the autumn to wintering grounds in warmer regions to the south
Glossary of bird terms.fact: The most common pattern involves flying north in the northern spring to breed in the temperate or Arctic summer, and returning in the autumn to wintering grounds in warmer regions to the south.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: For example, in Australia, _____ of non-passerine birds and 32% of passerine species are partially migratory
Glossary of bird terms.fact: For example, in Australia, 44% of non-passerine birds and 32% of passerine species are partially migratory.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: For larger birds, flying in flocks reduces the energy cost, e.g., geese in a V-formation may conserve 12–_____ of the energy they would otherwise need if flying alone
Glossary of bird terms.fact: For larger birds, flying in flocks reduces the energy cost, e.g., geese in a V-formation may conserve 12–20% of the energy they would otherwise need if flying alone.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: Because feathers make up 4–_____ of a bird's body weight, it takes a large amount of energy to replace them
Glossary of bird terms.fact: Because feathers make up 4–12% of a bird's body weight, it takes a large amount of energy to replace them.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: moult strategy _____ types defined: simple basic strategy; simple alternate strategy; complex basic strategy; complex alternate strategy
Glossary of bird terms.fact: moult strategy Specialized types defined: simple basic strategy; simple alternate strategy; complex basic strategy; complex alternate strategy.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery

Glossary of bird terms.fact: The smallest bird nests are those of some hummingbirds, tiny cups which can be a mere 2 cm (0.79 in) across and 2–3 cm (0.79–1.18 in) high.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: nidicolous _____ that remain in their nest after hatching for an extended period of time and thus must be fed by their parents
Glossary of bird terms.fact: nidicolous Young that remain in their nest after hatching for an extended period of time and thus must be fed by their parents. nidifugous Young that leave the nest soon after hatching, joining their parents in foraging.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: nidifugous _____ that leave the nest soon after hatching, joining their parents in foraging
Glossary of bird terms.fact: nidicolous Young that remain in their nest after hatching for an extended period of time and thus must be fed by their parents. nidifugous Young that leave the nest soon after hatching, joining their parents in foraging.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: Any bird of the order _____, which includes more than half of all bird species
Glossary of bird terms.fact: Any bird of the order Passeriformes, which includes more than half of all bird species.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery

Glossary of bird terms.fact: A notable feature of passerines compared to other orders of Aves is the arrangement of their toes—three pointing forward and one back—which facilitates perching.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: The order has roughly twice as many species as _____, the largest order of mammals
Glossary of bird terms.fact: The order has roughly twice as many species as Rodentia, the largest order of mammals.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: There are more than _____ families of passerine birds, the second-most of any tetrapods (after Squamata, the scaled reptiles)
Glossary of bird terms.fact: There are more than 110 families of passerine birds, the second-most of any tetrapods (after Squamata, the scaled reptiles).

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: pectoral tuft _____ feathers, often brightly coloured, which arise from the sides of the chest of some species of birds, including many sunbirds, spiderhunters and flowerpeckers
Glossary of bird terms.fact: pectoral tuft Elongated feathers, often brightly coloured, which arise from the sides of the chest of some species of birds, including many sunbirds, spiderhunters and flowerpeckers.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: plumage Plumage (_____: plūma 'feather') refers both to the layer of feathers that cover a bird and the pattern, colour and arrangement of those feathers
Glossary of bird terms.fact: plumage Plumage (Latin: plūma 'feather') refers both to the layer of feathers that cover a bird and the pattern, colour and arrangement of those feathers.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: "Prealternate moult" is used in _____–Parkes terminology, and "prenuptial moult" is the traditional term
Glossary of bird terms.fact: "Prealternate moult" is used in Humphrey–Parkes terminology, and "prenuptial moult" is the traditional term.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: In traditional terminology, the first is called the postjuvenal moult, and thereafter the _____st, 2nd, 3rd (etc.) postnuptial moult
Glossary of bird terms.fact: In Humphrey–Parkes terminology, prebasic moults in juveniles, prior to attaining definitive plumage, are numbered the 1st, 2nd, 3rd (etc.) prebasic moult. In traditional terminology, the first is called the postjuvenal moult, and thereafter the 1st, 2nd, 3rd (etc.) postnuptial moult.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: Feathers require maintenance and birds preen or groom them daily, spending an average of around _____ of their daily time on this activity
Glossary of bird terms.fact: Feathers require maintenance and birds preen or groom them daily, spending an average of around 9% of their daily time on this activity.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: psilopaedic _____ that are born naked or with only a small amount of down feather coverage, as opposed to birds that are ptilopaedic
Glossary of bird terms.fact: This allows these birds to either digest their food later or carry it back to their young. psilopaedic Young that are born naked or with only a small amount of down feather coverage, as opposed to birds that are ptilopaedic.

Glossary of bird terms.question: ptilopaedic _____ that are born covered with down feathers, as opposed to birds that are psilopaedic
Glossary of bird terms.fact: ptilopaedic Young that are born covered with down feathers, as opposed to birds that are psilopaedic.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: By contrast, in _____'s well known treatise, Ornithology, he writes at page 80: "The hollow base of the shaft—the calamus, or quill—anchors the feather in a follicle below the surface of the skin"
Glossary of bird terms.fact: By contrast, in Frank B. Gill's well known treatise, Ornithology, he writes at page 80: "The hollow base of the shaft—the calamus, or quill—anchors the feather in a follicle below the surface of the skin".

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
Glossary of bird terms.question: From the _____ for 'helmsman', they are the long, stiff, asymmetrically shaped, but symmetrically paired pennaceous feathers on the tail of a bird, which help it to brake and steer in flight
Glossary of bird terms.fact: From the Latin for 'helmsman', they are the long, stiff, asymmetrically shaped, but symmetrically paired pennaceous feathers on the tail of a bird, which help it to brake and steer in flight.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery

Glossary of bird terms.fact: From the Latin for 'oarsman', they are the long, stiff, asymmetrically shaped, but symmetrically paired pennaceous feathers on the wings of a bird.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery

Glossary of bird terms.fact: The remicle is very small and usually non-functional—interpreted by Christian Ludwig Nitzsch as "an aborted first primary".

Glossary of bird terms.fact: This covering arises from the Malpighian layer of the bird's epidermis, growing from plates at the base of each mandible.

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery

Glossary of bird terms.subject: Farm Machinery
